name: Segmentation artifact: truncation and container-label prefixes
instruction: Score 0-10 for HOW MUCH the text shows signs of having been cut out of a larger record rather than standing as a whole submission. 10 = the text is unmistakably a fragment: it breaks off mid-sentence or mid-phrase, ends in a bare dash or colon with nothing after it, or consists only of an item label carried over from the surrounding layout (e.g. a parenthetical figure label or a numbered quote header) with no body. 5 = the text is grammatically complete but opens with a carried-over label, prefix or numbering that is clearly part of the container's layout rather than of the entry. 0 = a clean, self-contained string with no layout residue and no truncation. Score the mechanical evidence of cutting only. You must NOT judge whether a fragment is a bad entry, and must not infer merit or its absence from the fragment's content.

name: Byline metadata residue
instruction: Rate from 0 to 10 how much the visible text includes appended author names, locations, or single-author parenthetical credits rather than entry content. Judge only extent; do not judge whether the credited author or entry is good.

name: Trailing furniture: hashtags, handles, parenthetical byline
instruction: Score 0-10 for how much non-sentence furniture is appended at the end of the text -- trailing hashtags, @-handles, a parenthetical name and town, or similar tags. 10 = several such tags appended; 0 = the text ends with the sentence itself. Count the furniture only; this is not a judgement of writing quality.

name: Coauthor signature
instruction: Score 0–10 for how much the text visibly signals multiple authors, joint credit, or collaborative production; do not judge whether collaboration improves the entry.

name: Reference With Comic Function
instruction: Score 10 when a cultural or personal reference actively creates the joke’s tension or reversal; score 0 when the reference is merely decorative or obscure without comic work.

name: Extent of capitalised or shouted typography
instruction: Score 0-10 for how much of the text is set in capital letters or otherwise typographically shouted (ALL-CAPS words, repeated letters, strings of exclamation marks). 10 = the text is dominated by shouted typography; 0 = ordinary sentence case throughout. Count the typography only; do not judge whether it is good or whether the item is funny.

name: Logical Collapse Depth
instruction: Score 10 when a statement initially sounds sensible but fails under a specific second reading; score 0 when it is a truism, tautology, or merely grammatical statement.

name: Vivid Comic Scene
instruction: Score 10 when the wording creates a specific, easily pictured situation that carries the humor; score 0 when it remains an abstract label or unelaborated assertion.

name: Found phrase reframed rather than invented
instruction: Score whether the entry takes an existing, unaltered phrase from the world and makes it funny purely by placing it in the contest's frame. 10 = the phrase is quoted exactly as it exists in ordinary use, and the entire comic work is done by the new frame, which reveals a property the phrase always had but nobody had named. 5 = an existing phrase is used but with modification or added scaffolding. 0 = the entry manufactures a novel string that has no life outside this entry. Note that this criterion can be high while surface effort looks near zero.

name: A specific concrete detail carries the joke
instruction: Score 0-10 for whether the comic work is done by a specific, concrete particular (a named thing, an exact number, a precise action) rather than by a generic category word. 10 = one vivid particular is doing the work; 0 = only generic labels, nothing specific enough to picture. Judge the specificity of the comic content, not the length.

name: Joint-byline and recurring-name fingerprint in the credit
instruction: Score 0-10 for HOW STRONGLY the visible credit apparatus signals a practised or collaborating submitter rather than a one-off individual. 10 = two or more named submitters sharing one entry, a household pair, or a semicolon-joined multi-person credit. 5 = a single named submitter whose name or locality is formatted with unusual completeness (middle initial, out-of-state qualifier, formal styling). 0 = a plain single name, or no credit at all. Score only what the credit string looks like. You must NOT judge whether collaboration or practice is good, must not speculate about the person's skill, and must not let this affect any read on the entry's humour.

name: Cliché Reassignment
instruction: Score 10 when a familiar slogan, quotation, or title is relocated so its usual implication becomes newly comic; score 0 when the familiar phrase remains unchanged or is attached arbitrarily.

name: Formal-structure discipline (meter/rhyme/reversal precision)
instruction: For entries constrained by a named literary form (limerick, chiasmus, Tom Swifty, haiku, etc.), score 0-10 how precisely and cleanly the entry satisfies that form's meter, rhyme scheme, grammatical reversal, or other structural constraint. 10 = the form is executed with no metrical, rhyme, or structural flaws. 0 = the form is badly broken, ignored, or barely attempted.

name: Contest-Aware Metahumor
instruction: Score 10 when the entry comments on contests, media, or the act of submitting humor while remaining a functioning joke; score 0 when it is a generic statement unrelated to that machinery.

name: Morphological wordplay
instruction: Rate from 0 (absent) to 10 (pervasive) how much the entry uses spelling changes, homophones, portmanteaus, or near-word substitutions. Judge only extent; do not judge whether the wordplay is good, funny, or effective.

name: Readable Contradiction
instruction: Score 10 when an apparent contradiction follows from a precise, instantly understandable clash of meanings; score 0 when it is merely short, technically paradoxical, or semantically arbitrary.

name: Interrogative/question-form surface syntax
instruction: Score 0-10 how much the entry's surface syntax takes question form (begins with an interrogative word such as 'What,' 'Who,' 'Why,' or 'How,' and/or ends with a question mark). 0 = entry is not phrased as a question at all; 10 = entry is fully phrased as a direct question in both opening word and terminal punctuation. Score only this surface syntactic feature; do not judge whether the question itself is clever.

name: Mutual Semantic Lock
instruction: Score 10 when the entry’s parts make one another newly meaningful or surprising; score 0 when its parts merely coexist without a reciprocal connection.

name: Crude/taboo content as sole comedic engine
instruction: Score 0-10 how much the entry's laugh depends on scatological, sexual, or taboo subject matter carrying the joke essentially by itself, with little additional wit layered on top. 10 = shock/crude content alone is doing nearly all the work. 0 = no reliance on taboo content; humor (if any) comes from elsewhere.

name: Multi-layered simultaneous wordplay
instruction: Score 0-10 how many distinct, independent meanings or resonances the entry's central wordplay activates at once. 10 = the pun/phrase works on two or more genuinely separate semantic layers simultaneously (e.g. it is literally true of the referenced person's public reputation AND fits the contest's formal template AND carries a secondary double meaning). 0 = a single flat, one-layer substitution with no secondary resonance beyond the obvious swap.

name: Raw length, clause count and syntactic elaboration
instruction: Score 0-10 for HOW LONG and syntactically elaborated the text is, in absolute terms. 10 = multiple sentences or many subordinate clauses, roughly 30 words or more, with embedded qualifications. 5 = one full sentence of ordinary length. 0 = a bare phrase of one to three words. Count words and clauses; ignore verse line breaks and count the running text. You must NOT judge whether the length is appropriate to the format, whether the text is padded or economical, or whether brevity is a virtue here. This is a raw size measurement.

name: Self-demonstrating execution (the entry enacts its own claim)
instruction: Score whether the entry performs the property it is talking about, so that its form and its content collide. 10 = the text is an instance of the very thing it names or denies, and the collision is the joke (e.g. a word that violates its own definition, a statement whose confident structure is exactly what makes its content vacuous). 5 = form and content are consistent but the form adds a small extra layer. 0 = form is a neutral container for the content. Score the collision, not general cleverness.

name: Sets up an expectation and then turns it
instruction: Score 0-10 for whether the wording first leads the reader toward one reading and then supplies a different one. 10 = a clear setup and a clear turn away from it; 0 = a single flat statement with no setup and nothing turned. Judge the comic structure, not the typography.

name: Dated cultural anchoring
instruction: Rate from 0 to 10 how much the entry depends on period-bound people, technologies, institutions, or media, such as obsolete devices or strongly era-specific references. Judge only extent; do not judge whether the references are good or funny.

name: Proper-name density
instruction: Score 0–10 for how densely the entry contains named people, places, institutions, brands, songs, or titles; count visible entities only and do not judge their appropriateness.

name: In-group reference to the column and its rituals
instruction: Score 0-10 for HOW MUCH the text refers to the contest itself, its running jokes, its recurring apparatus, or the experience of entering it, as opposed to referring only to the world outside. 10 = the column, its prizes, its rituals, its regulars or its self-mocking house identity are the explicit subject of the text. 5 = a passing venue-insider allusion or a coinage that only parses to someone who reads the column regularly. 0 = no reference to the contest or its community anywhere in the text. Score presence and prominence of the in-group reference only. You must NOT judge whether the self-reference is charming, tiresome, or well-executed, and must not treat insider fluency as evidence of quality.

name: Perspective Reversal
instruction: Score 10 when the entry makes a familiar institution, relationship, or activity absurd by shifting the reader’s viewpoint; score 0 when it merely describes an odd object or situation.

name: Economy: comedic payoff per word
instruction: Score 0-10 the ratio of comedic payoff to text length: how much of the joke's full effect is delivered in very few words versus requiring a long wind-up to reach a comparably small payoff. 10 = maximal payoff landed in a handful of words. 0 = long entry required to arrive at a comparably small or absent payoff.

name: Topical/biographical knowledge required to resolve joke
instruction: Score 0-10 how much the entry's comedic payoff depends on the reader already knowing a specific real-world scandal, event, or fact tied to a named person or institution, versus being resolvable purely from the words on the page. 10 = the entry is inert or meaningless without that outside knowledge. 0 = fully self-contained; no external knowledge of any specific event is needed.
